summary: Evaluate the three exponentially rescaled modified Bessel quantities the relativistic background-Maxwellian branch of the Coulomb collision coefficient chain needs: exp(x)K_0(x), exp(x)K_1(x), and the K_2 recurrence. The retained route's piecewise Abramowitz-Stegun approximation is replaced by a direct evaluation of the relation, which removes a 1.5e-3 relative discontinuity at the approximation's x = 2 branch boundary and removes the branch selector, branch label and per-branch accuracy metadata from the public contract. Every accepted call returns three finite floats; a valid argument for which the double-precision backend does not produce them is rejected rather than answered with a non-finite value.
aliases: rescaled modified Bessel K0 K1 K2

identity.relation: the Bessel argument to the exponentially rescaled modified Bessel quantities of orders zero, one and two
identity.definition: Returns bk0 = exp(x)*K_0(x) and bk1 = exp(x)*K_1(x) evaluated directly, and bk2 = bk0 + 2*bk1/x, which is the K_2 recurrence and not an independent third approximation. The three values are computed and then checked once for finiteness; the call is rejected if any of them is not finite.
identity.model: exact rescaled modified Bessel functions of the second kind; no approximation and no branch
identity.geometry: not applicable; a scalar special-function evaluation
identity.boundary: as x approaches zero from above, bk0 tends to -log(x/2) - gamma and bk1 grows as 1/x, so bk2 grows as 2/x^2; as x grows, all three quantities decay as sqrt(pi/(2x))
assumptions: The argument is a positive finite scalar; the rescaled form exp(x)*K_order(x) is the quantity of interest because the unrescaled K_order(x) underflows over the range the closure is used at.

The K_2 recurrence is an identity for the true functions, so bk2 is defined by the recurrence rather than evaluated as a third independent approximation; the two agree to the last bit over the domain measured.

The relation is evaluated through scipy.special.kve, a double-precision routine whose representable domain is finite. The extent of that domain is a property of the installed SciPy build and the platform, not of the relation, so this asset states no bound for it and imposes no upper or lower bound of its own.

An argument the backend cannot evaluate is a backend failure rather than an input error: the caller's argument satisfies every stated precondition, and the caller can do nothing about the outcome except handle the rejection.
No physical accuracy claim is made: the closure is established as the rescaled Bessel functions, not as an adequate model for any particular distribution.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: Bessel argument of the rescaled modified Bessel functions.
inputs.constraints: Strictly positive and finite. No upper or lower bound is imposed beyond that; an argument the backend cannot evaluate is rejected as a backend failure rather than as an invalid input.

outputs.name: bk0
outputs.description: exp(x) times the modified Bessel function of the second kind of order zero.
outputs.constraints: A finite Python float on every accepted call.

outputs.name: bk1
outputs.description: exp(x) times the modified Bessel function of the second kind of order one.
outputs.constraints: A finite Python float on every accepted call.

outputs.name: bk2
outputs.constraints: Equals bk0 + 2*bk1/x exactly, and is a finite Python float on every accepted call. An argument at which the recurrence's 2*bk1/x term is not representable is rejected rather than answered with an infinity.

preconditions: The caller wants the rescaled form exp(x)*K_order(x), which is the form the relativistic Maxwellian branch needs.
The argument is a positive finite scalar.
The installed SciPy can evaluate scipy.special.kve at the argument; the caller cannot determine this in advance from this asset, which states no bound for it.
supported: Any positive finite argument the installed backend evaluates, including arguments spanning the removed approximation's x = 2 branch boundary.
The recurrence definition of bk2 and its agreement with the direct order-two value.
Distinguishing a malformed argument from an argument the backend could not evaluate, through the two rejection classes.
excluded: Any physical accuracy claim for a distribution, temperature or relativistic parameter.
Unrescaled K_order(x), which underflows over the range of interest.
Orders other than zero, one and two.
A caller-selectable approximation branch or accuracy bound; those were V2 public contract and are removed.
Any statement of the backend's representable domain, which is a property of the installed SciPy rather than of the relation.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises InvalidBesselArgumentError, a subclass of ValueError, when the argument is not strictly positive and finite, with the retained route's message. This is the retained route's guard, unchanged; only the exception class is narrowed so a caller can tell its own mistake from a backend failure.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises BesselBackendEvaluationError, also a subclass of ValueError, when the argument is valid and scipy.special.kve did not return three finite quantities for it. The message reports the argument and the three values produced. It states no domain bound and names no threshold, because the argument at which a given SciPy build stops returning finite values is a property of that build and platform rather than of the relation. The rejection is whole-call: a partially non-finite closure is not a usable scientific result.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this operator has no iteration or feedback.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; a rejected call produces no mapping.

provenance.lineage_summary: SciRel-owned formalisation of the retained CQL3D L1 route 相对论MaxwellianBessel闭合, which the bundle anchors on cfpmodbe.f. The retained route evaluates the closure through the Abramowitz-Stegun piecewise polynomial fits split at x = 2: below the split, the I0/I1 fits and the small-argument K0/K1 series rescaled by exp(x); at and above it, the asymptotic polynomials in 2/x. The two branches represent the same function but do not meet, and the measured bk1 discontinuity at the boundary, 1.5076691838017936e-03 relative, is larger than the route's smooth approximation error anywhere in its domain. This candidate evaluates the relation directly and therefore does not reproduce the retained route's arithmetic; it reproduces the relation the route approximates, to within the route's own approximation error away from the boundary. This candidate is derived from the V2 review unit of the same name through the V3 review unit: V2 kept the approximation and added a measured near-minimax branch selector, a branch label and per-branch accuracy bounds as public outputs, all three of which V3 removed; V3 also disclosed the direct evaluation's reduced domain and returned non-finite values through it, and V4 replaces that disclosure with a fail-closed rejection. The retained bundle cites no reference for the coefficients or for the split, and states no licence.

example.description: Evaluate the closure at the removed approximation's branch boundary and one ulp below it, confirm that the two agree to rounding rather than jumping by 1.5e-3, confirm the three returned quantities are the rescaled Bessel functions with bk2 the recurrence, confirm that every accepted value is finite, and confirm that a malformed argument and a backend failure are distinguishable.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy.special import kve
from scirel.collisions import (
    BesselBackendEvaluationError,
    InvalidBesselArgumentError,
    relativistic_maxwellian_bessel,
)
boundary = 2.0
below = float(np.nextafter(boundary, -np.inf))
at = relativistic_maxwellian_bessel(boundary)
near = relativistic_maxwellian_bessel(below)
assert set(at) == {'bk0', 'bk1', 'bk2'}
assert all(type(value) is float for value in at.values())
assert all(np.isfinite(value) for value in at.values())
assert at['bk0'] == float(kve(0, boundary))
assert at['bk1'] == float(kve(1, boundary))
assert at['bk2'] == at['bk0'] + 2.0 * at['bk1'] / boundary
jump = abs(near['bk1'] - at['bk1']) / abs(at['bk1'])
assert jump == 8.59408144671376e-16
assert jump < 1.0e-12
for good in (1.0e-3, 0.5, 1.0, 60.0, 700.0):
    assert all(np.isfinite(value) for value in relativistic_maxwellian_bessel(good).values())
try:
    relativistic_maxwellian_bessel(0.0)
except InvalidBesselArgumentError as error:
    assert 'positive and finite' in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError('a non-positive argument must be rejected')
assert issubclass(InvalidBesselArgumentError, ValueError)
assert issubclass(BesselBackendEvaluationError, ValueError)
example.expected: bk0, bk1 and bk2 for x = 2 equal to scipy.special.kve(0, 2), kve(1, 2) and the recurrence bk0 + 2*bk1/2, all finite Python floats; the relative bk1 difference across the branch boundary is 8.59408144671376e-16, where the retained route jumps by 1.5076691838017936e-03; every accepted argument in the sample returns three finite floats; and a non-positive argument raises InvalidBesselArgumentError, with both rejection classes being ValueError subclasses. The example makes no claim about where the backend stops returning finite values, because that is a property of the installed SciPy rather than of the relation.

scope: How this evidence is organised. The frozen V5 review established every claim below by comparing this asset against external arms -- the retained source route and the frozen V2 and V3 candidates -- which live outside this repository and are reachable only in the review environment. The maintained tests in this repository replay none of those comparisons and depend on no source checkout, no candidate directory and no L1 payload. They protect the claims that are self-contained: the public relation's own runtime behaviour, its input and failure contracts, and its regression values. Where a claim rests on an external comparison it is recorded here as the frozen review's finding and is marked as not replayed by the maintained tests.

How this evidence is organised (2/2). The maintained suite is tests/operator_contracts/test_relativistic_maxwellian_bessel.py, and it is self-contained: it imports nothing outside SciRel, SciPy, NumPy and pytest, and it exercises the fail-closed contract by substituting the backend for the duration of a test rather than by probing where the installed SciPy stops being representable.

That the closure returns exactly the three rescaled Bessel quantities. Protected by the maintained tests, which assert the returned mapping's keys are exactly bk0, bk1 and bk2 for arguments spanning the removed boundary. Frozen review finding: the V2 candidate returned six keys, adding the branch label, the applied switch and the per-branch accuracy bounds. Not replayed.

That the signature is the retained route's single positional argument. Protected by the maintained tests, which assert the parameter list is exactly ('x',) and that a branch_switch keyword raises TypeError. Frozen review finding: the V2 candidate had added that keyword. Not replayed.

The removal of the branch discontinuity. Frozen review finding: both the retained route and the V2 candidate jump by 1.5076691838017936e-03 relative in bk1 across x = 2, which is the retained route's own stated per-branch accuracy bound and the largest error in its domain. Not replayed, because those arms are unreachable from here. Protected by the maintained tests as the property the removal buys: this asset's own jump at x = 2 is 8.59408144671376e-16, within the rounding scale of two adjacent doubles, and the closure is smooth across every sampled neighbourhood rather than at that one point.
That bk0 and bk1 are exactly scipy.special.kve(0, x) and kve(1, x) at arguments spanning the removed boundary. Protected by the maintained tests directly.
That bk2 is the K_2 recurrence evaluated exactly as bk0 + 2*bk1/x and agrees with the direct order-two value. Protected by the maintained tests directly.

That away from the boundary the two routes agree to the retained approximation's own accuracy. Frozen review finding: the worst relative differences from the retained route were 1.4592152808791253e-07 for bk0, 0.0007518301076547563 for bk1 and 0.00042540348489499393 for bk2, over 40000 points spanning (0, 1.9] and [2.1, 60]. Not replayed, because the retained route is unreachable from here. Recorded because it is what establishes that the change is the approximation rather than the relation.

The fail-closed contract, established by making the backend return NaN and Inf rather than by probing where the installed SciPy stops: the call raises BesselBackendEvaluationError for a non-finite bk0, bk1 or bk2, including when only the recurrence overflows. Protected by the maintained tests, which substitute the backend so the failure is unconditional and identical on every platform.

That the rejection message states the argument and the values produced and contains no domain bound, threshold or direction claim. Protected by the maintained tests, which read the message and assert the absence of every bound-shaped word.

That the implementation carries no backend threshold: no such constant, attribute or measured literal appears in the module. Protected by the maintained tests, which check the module's attributes and its source for the literals the V3 candidate pinned.

That the two rejection classes are distinguishable and that both are ValueError subclasses, so a caller that only knows ValueError still catches everything the relation raises. Protected by the maintained tests directly.

The retained route's input contract, unchanged: a non-positive or non-finite argument raises the retained message, and a non-numeric argument is still a TypeError rather than either rejection class. Frozen review finding: the retained route raises the same message. Protected here directly against the public callable.

That every accepted call in a wide logarithmic sweep returns three finite Python floats. Protected by the maintained tests over 4000 arguments, which treat a backend rejection as a legitimate outcome rather than a failure.
The rescaled-function identity and the asymptotic form, and the monotone decrease of bk0 and bk1 in x. Protected by the maintained tests directly, independently of either route.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Establishes, on the frozen review's external comparison, the measured distance from the retained route and from its boundary discontinuity, and that the change is the approximation rather than the relation. Establishes, on the maintained self-contained tests, that the closure is the exponentially rescaled modified Bessel functions of orders zero, one and two, that bk2 is the recurrence, that every accepted call returns three finite floats, and the response to a backend that does not return finite values. The maintained tests depend on no source checkout, candidate directory or L1 payload. This asset does not establish the physical accuracy of the closure for any distribution, temperature or relativistic parameter, does not establish or bound the domain over which the installed backend can evaluate the relation, does not establish that the retained Abramowitz-Stegun coefficients or its x = 2 split were the right ones to have replaced, and consults no independent special-function table.
known_limitations: The relation is evaluated through scipy.special.kve, so this asset has a runtime dependency on SciPy that the retained route did not have. That is the point of the change, but it is a dependency the caller inherits.

The direct evaluation's representable domain is a property of the installed SciPy build and the platform, and is narrower than the retained route's, whose asymptotic polynomial stays finite at arguments where the backend does not. This asset states no bound for it, deliberately: a bound measured from one build would be a false contract on another. A caller that needs one must derive it from its own platform, and a caller that samples a wide argument range must handle BesselBackendEvaluationError.
Rejection is whole-call and gives the caller no partial result, so a caller sweeping many arguments must decide per argument whether to skip it.
No physical accuracy claim is made for any distribution. The closure is established as a special-function evaluation, not as an adequate collision-coefficient model.
The retained route's coefficients, its choice of Abramowitz-Stegun fits and its x = 2 split are taken as given; the bundle cites no reference for any of them.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.

The frozen V5 review's comparisons against the retained route and the frozen V2 and V3 candidates are not replayable from this repository: those arms live outside it, and the maintained tests neither reach them nor depend on them. The claims they established are recorded in this document's verification scope and marked as not replayed; a reviewer who needs to re-check them must return to the frozen review environment. The maintained tests protect the self-contained subset, and no public test requires an external checkout.
